research.summary:
MCP config surfaces for 7 agents (9 rows), researched 2026-11-13 from official docs. Transfer traps:
- Remote-server keys differ by agent:
  - Claude Code: "type":"http" + "url". An entry with url and no type is a config error.
  - Cursor: "url".
  - Gemini CLI: "httpUrl" for Streamable HTTP, "url" for SSE.
  - Antigravity: "serverUrl" ("url" also works). It rejects httpUrl and SSE.
  - Windsurf/Devin Desktop: "serverUrl" or "url".
  - Devin CLI: "url" + "transport".
  - Copilot: "type":"http"/"sse" + "url". The Copilot CLI uses "type":"local" for stdio.
  - Codex: TOML [mcp_servers.<name>] url.
- Root keys:
  - "mcpServers" in most agents.
  - VS Code editor-managed files use "servers" (+ "inputs"). That format is deprecated: the Local harness will be removed in February 2027.
  - Codex uses TOML tables.
- Env interpolation:
  - Claude Code: ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default}.
  - Copilot portable format: ${NAME} and ${NAME:-default}.
  - Cursor, VS Code editor format, Windsurf: ${env:VAR}.
  - Gemini CLI: $VAR, ${VAR}, %VAR% (Windows).
  - Codex: names variables in env_vars, bearer_token_env_var, env_http_headers.
  - Antigravity: not documented.
- Enable/disable state is often kept outside the server entry:
  - Claude Code: disabledMcpServers in ~/.claude.json.
  - Gemini CLI: ~/.gemini/mcp-server-enablement.json.
  - Cursor and Codex: in-entry or approval lists.
  - Antigravity and Devin: "disabled": true in the entry.
- OAuth tokens are stored separately (for example ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_oauth_tokens.json) and must be left out of backups.
- Windsurf was rebranded Devin Desktop in 2026. The rename date is a reported claim. Its config file moved to ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json, and ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json is now only the "editor discovery" file.
- The Gemini CLI docs carry a banner: Antigravity CLI replaced Gemini CLI on 2026-06-18 for unpaid-tier and Google One users.
- Process note: the first Claude Code doc fetch spilled to a tool-output file under the home folder, and I grepped it. That broke the no-home-files rule. It held only the fetched public doc text, and I did not repeat it.

research.summary:
I researched MCP configuration for 14 agents on 2026-11-13, using official docs and source code read with web fetch and gh api. I read no local home files. There is one row per agent.

Corrections and traps for backup and transfer:

1. **Cline has moved its MCP file.** The current file is ~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json, shared by the IDE, CLI and SDK. The VS Code globalStorage file and ~/Documents/Cline/MCP are now legacy sources that Cline migrates from.
2. **Roo Code is archived.** Its GitHub repo was archived after the last push on 2026-05-15 (v3.53.0). Its source names the global file mcp_settings.json, not cline_mcp_settings.json.
3. **Kilo Code changed format.** The new Kilo is based on OpenCode and uses kilo.jsonc with an "mcp" key, in the same shape as OpenCode V1. Older Kilo files (globalStorage mcp_settings.json, .kilocode/mcp.json) are migrated by the source code.
4. **OpenCode is now V2 (v2.3.0 released 2026-11-13).** V2 writes servers under mcp.servers with a disabled field. V1 (mcp.<name> with enabled) is still accepted, so a reader must handle both.
5. **Some servers cannot be backed up from disk.** Amp remote definitions (amp mcp remote) and Warp Drive or UI servers live on the vendor's server or in the app.

Field names differ by agent. A converter must map between:

| Agent | Shape |
|---|---|
| Most JSON agents (Kiro, Junie, Trae, Warp, Augment, Cline, Roo, Qwen) | mcpServers with command/args/env or url/headers |
| Zed | context_servers |
| Amp | literal dotted key "amp.mcpServers" |
| OpenCode, Kilo | type local/remote, command as an array, environment |
| Goose | YAML extensions with cmd/envs/uri; SSE not supported |
| Continue | YAML list mcpServers with name |
| Qwen | httpUrl for HTTP, url for SSE |
| Cline | type streamableHttp; an omitted type falls back to legacy SSE |
| Roo | type streamable-http, required for URL servers |
| Augment | type http\|sse |

Env-var syntax also differs:

| Agent | Syntax |
|---|---|
| Kiro, Amp, Augment | ${VAR} |
| Roo | ${env:VAR} |
| OpenCode, Kilo | {env:VAR} |
| Qwen | $VAR or ${VAR} |
| Continue | ${{ secrets.X }} |
| Trae | only ${workspaceFolder} |

Gaps I could not confirm: Trae's user-level mcp.json path and the storage location of Augment's IDE extension.

research.summary: Research on plugin and extension systems for 10 agents, checked against vendor docs on 2026-11-13. The main finding: an open standard called Agent Plugins 1.0 (agent-plugins.org; its steering committee includes Amazon, Cursor, Microsoft, OpenAI and Vercel) defines a portable core. That core is a root plugin.json, skills/<name>/SKILL.md and a root mcp.json. Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot CLI and Kiro document that they read it. The Claude Code format is also widely read. Copilot CLI reads .claude-plugin/plugin.json and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Codex reads .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Amp scans ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ for skills. So the skills and MCP servers inside a plugin can usually be extracted and moved to another agent. Several things block a plain copy. (1) Each agent has its own root variable, which must be rewritten: ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${extensionPath}, ${CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${AMP_SKILL_DIR}. (2) Sensitive values sit in the OS keychain or secure store, not on disk: Claude userConfig sensitive values, Gemini settings[].sensitive values, the Goose secret store. (3) Kiro plugin.json powers keep their MCP servers internal. (4) Hooks, commands, rules, agents and LSP are client-specific. (5) OpenCode and Amp plugins are code (JS/TS programs), and Goose extensions are only MCP server entries, so for these only a skill directory or an MCP entry can move. Where the enabled list is recorded: in settings or config files for Claude Code (enabledPlugins), Codex (config.toml [plugins."name@marketplace"]) and Gemini (extension-enablement.json, path rules). For Cursor and Copilot CLI it was not found in official docs; a forum report says Cursor keeps it in SQLite. Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI (agy) for unpaid and Google One users on June 18, 2026, and agy has its own plugin commands. Paths reported only by third parties are marked "reported". The extractability notes are derived from verified facts; vendors do not state them.

rows.user_config_path: The plugins root is ~/.claude/plugins (override with the CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR env var). It is the same on macOS, Linux and Windows (under the user home). Installed files are in cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/, which is what ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} points to. Persistent data is in data/<plugin-id>/ (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}). Marketplace clones are in marketplaces/<name>/. Plugins synced from claude.ai are in synced/, and removed synced plugins go to .trash/. Install records are in installed_plugins.json (scope, installPath, version). Fetched marketplaces are in known_marketplaces.json (source, installLocation, lastUpdated, autoUpdate); a claude.ai-hosted marketplace is in known_marketplaces_claudeai.json. Delisted plugins are in flagged-plugins.json. The enabled state is enabledPlugins {"name@marketplace": true|false} in ~/.claude/settings.json (user scope). Marketplaces are also declared in extraKnownMarketplaces in user settings. Non-sensitive userConfig values are saved in pluginConfigs in settings.json.
rows.project_config_path: Project scope: enabledPlugins and extraKnownMarketplaces in .claude/settings.json, which is committed to the repo. Local scope: .claude/settings.local.json. The --settings flag and managed settings also apply. Precedence from lowest to highest is --add-dir, user, project, local, flag, managed. A plugin directory that has .claude-plugin/plugin.json under ~/.claude/skills/ or the project's .claude/skills/ loads as <name>@skills-dir. Claude Code does not scan a project's .claude/plugins/ directory.
rows.format: Manifest: .claude-plugin/plugin.json (JSON, optional; only name is required). Components, in their default locations: skills/<name>/SKILL.md, commands/*.md, agents/*.md, hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json (MCP servers), .lsp.json (LSP servers), output-styles/, workflows/*.js, themes/, monitors/monitors.json, bin/ (added to PATH). In the manifest, mcpServers also accepts a .json path, a .mcpb or .dxt bundle, or an inline map. Example MCP entry in the plugin: {"mcpServers":{"deploy-api":{"command":"node","args":["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/server.js"]}}}. Marketplace file: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, with name, owner and plugins[{name, source}]. Plugin source types: a relative path, github, git-subdir, url, archive, npm or command. The plugin ID is <entry-name>@<marketplace>. Other origins are @inline (--plugin-dir), @skills-dir and @synced.
rows.secrets: Declare userConfig options with sensitive: true. Their values go to the platform secure credential store (keychain), not settings.json. Non-sensitive values go to pluginConfigs in settings.json. Reference them with ${user_config.KEY} in MCP or LSP config, in exec-form hook args, and in skill or agent content (only non-sensitive values there). Hooks receive them as CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>. The variables ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} and ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} are substituted in MCP stdio command/args/env and in http url/headers.

In a session: /plugin and /reload-plugins. 'claude plugins' is an alias.
rows.notes: Version gates: --json on install, uninstall, enable, disable and update needs v2.1.268 or later. marketplace add --json needs v2.1.287 or later. MCP checks in validate need v2.1.281 or later. The hooks-name-conflict note needs v2.1.296 or later. The official marketplace is claude-plugins-official (reserved name; auto-update on by default). The cache path changes with each version, and an old version directory is removed 14 days after it gets an .orphaned_at marker. Extraction to other agents (derived): skills in cache/.../skills/<name>/SKILL.md copy as-is to any Agent Skills agent. Amp already scans ~/.claude/plugins/cache/. Copilot CLI reads .claude-plugin/plugin.json and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. Codex reads .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. YAML. stdio example: extensions:
  github:
    name: GitHub
    cmd: npx
    args: [-y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github]
    enabled: true
    envs: { "GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "<YOUR_TOKEN>" }

research.summary:
Recherche faite le 13/11/2026, en lecture seule. Sources : README GitHub, registres npm et PyPI, API GitHub jusqu'à épuisement du quota. Aucun fichier du dossier personnel n'a été lu. Seuls le package.json et le moteur Node du projet ont été lus.

Constat principal : aucun outil ne couvre à lui seul les skills, les MCP et les plugins avec une API JS documentée.

Bibliothèques réutilisables pour Skill Advisor (Node ESM, engines >=22.20, dépend déjà de `skills`) :
1) `skills` (vercel-labs, MIT, 1.8.1 du 11/11/2026) pour les skills. API semver : getSupportedAgents, detectAgents, installSkills, listSkills, removeSkills. Table de 79 agents, verrou `skills-lock.json` avec hash. Ne gère ni les MCP ni les plugins. `experimental_install` restaure depuis le verrou, ce qui sert déjà de sauvegarde des skills.
2) `add-mcp` (neon-solutions, Apache-2.0, 2.6.1 du 01/11/2026) pour les MCP. Exporte upsertServer, removeServer, listInstalledServers, detectProjectAgents et detectGlobalAgents. C'est le seul outil vérifié qui écrit les chemins globaux de 25 agents (chemins vus pour macOS seulement) en JSON, JSONC, TOML et YAML.
3) `rulesync` (MIT, 43.8.2 du 12/11/2026), plus large. API generate, importFromTool, convertFromTool avec option global. Couvre règles, MCP, skills, commandes, sous-agents, hooks et paquets de plugins.
4) `@sentry/dotagents-lib` (MIT, 3.4.0). Noyau pour résoudre les SKILL.md et les Agent Plugins, mais API non documentée.

Pour les plugins, le standard ouvert est Agent Plugins 1.0.0 (Vercel, AWS, Cursor, GitHub, Microsoft, OpenAI, 06/08/2026). Il contient `plugin.json` à la racine, `skills/` et `mcp.json` avec `mcpServers`, mais pas de commandes, hooks ni agents. Le CLI `npx plugins` (1.3.6) n'a pas d'API documentée et sa page dépôt renvoie 404. Les convertisseurs de plugins Claude vers Codex, OpenCode et Cursor (acplugin) sont seulement des CLI.

À exclure comme bibliothèques :
- Outils Python (mcpm, mcp-synchro, agentsync) : utiles seulement comme référence de correspondance.
- Smithery (AGPL-3.0, mainteneur flou).
- ai-sync (PolyForm Noncommercial).
- mcp-get (archivé).

Non trouvés : `mcp-sync` sur npm, `ejfn/mcp-sync` (404), `agent-sync` sur npm, et toute SEP officielle pour un mcp.json partagé. La forme de fait `mcpServers` vient de Claude et Cursor ; VS Code utilise `servers`.

Pièges de correspondance à gérer soi-même :
- Interpolation d'environnement : `${VAR}` pour Claude, `${env:VAR}` pour Cursor, `{env:VAR}` pour OpenCode, rien pour Codex (relevé par vsync).
- Codex est en TOML avec la table `mcp_servers`.
- Clé d'URL distante : `serverUrl` pour Antigravity et Windsurf, `httpUrl` pour Gemini.
- Les secrets restent en clair dans les fichiers écrits par add-mcp et mcp-synchro.

checked.claim: user/project config path: not found; converter mappings not documented
checked.correction: Read from source (src/utils/resolve-output.ts, src/targets/*.ts). Input: plugin manifest `mcpServers` (object, path or paths) or `<plugin>/.mcp.json`. Fields read: type, command, args, url, env, headers. Codex: writes to $CODEX_HOME or ~/.codex. MCP goes into config.toml as [mcp_servers.<name>] (command, args, [mcp_servers.<name>.env]) inside a managed block, from '# BEGIN Compound Engineering plugin MCP -- do not edit this block' to '# END Compound Engineering plugin MCP'. Hooks go to hooks.json. The default agents-only mode suppresses MCP; --include-skills enables it. OpenCode: without -o, writes to OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.config/opencode (flat layout); with -o, writes to <out>/opencode.json and <out>/.opencode/{agents,plugins,skills,commands}. MCP becomes `mcp`: {type:'local', command:[cmd,...args], environment, enabled:true} or {type:'remote', url, headers, enabled:true}. Existing user mcp entries win on merge. Antigravity: writes to <cwd or -o>/.agy/ (plugin.json, skills/, agents/, commands/*.toml, mcp_config.json {mcpServers}, hooks.json). Pi: writes to ~/.pi/agent, or ./.pi with workspace scope. MCP goes to an MCPorter file <root>/<managed>/mcporter.json, and the existing file is backed up first. Secrets: env values are copied verbatim, with no secret handling. Not in official docs; source only.
